hypothesis.title: email memory leak causes GC pressure, OOMKills, and checkout latency spike
hypothesis.summary: The email service is experiencing a memory leak that started ~33 minutes before the alert. Memory grew from 33% to 93.5%, triggering heap pressure warnings and three OOMKill restarts. Each restart cycle causes email's p95 latency to spike from 59ms to over 1.3s due to GC pressure. Since checkout synchronously calls email for every order, this added 856ms to checkout's p95, breaching the 1.5s SLO.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired for checkout latency, but checkout itself shows healthy CPU (17-20%) and memory (41%). The trace analysis shows email accounts for 100% of the added latency (+856ms). Following the evidence to email: pod/email-c9e64536-3d55e has been OOMKilled 3 times, memory utilization climbed from 33% to 93.5% over the alert window, and logs show "heap usage above 90% after full GC" starting 33 minutes before the alert, plus fatal memory allocation errors. Email's p95 latency spiked from 59ms to 1.3s, matching the pattern. The payment 2.0.3 deploy happened 23 minutes before the alert, but payment is not on the critical path for the slow traces shown (trace 356ed282af89 shows checkout→email only), and there's no evidence of payment errors or latency. This matches PM-2026-05-04 (recommendation OOM loop): sawtooth memory growth, OOMKills, and latency degradation before each restart. The root cause is a memory leak in email causing GC pressure and eventual OOMKills.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: Email pod has been OOMKilled 3 times, confirming memory exhaustion is causing restarts and service disruption.
Memory grew from 33% to 93.5% over the alert window, showing a clear leak pattern rather than a one-time spike.
420 warnings of heap usage above 90% after full GC starting 33m before alert indicate GC pressure is causing latency before OOMKills.
Email accounts for 100% of the added latency in checkout traces (+856ms), proving email is the origin of checkout's latency problem.
Email p95 latency spiked from 59ms to 1.3s, correlating with memory pressure and explaining the checkout latency increase.
Fatal memory allocation errors confirm the service is hitting hard memory limits, not just GC pressure.

suggested_actions.title: Restart email deployment to temporarily restore service
suggested_actions.rationale: This will clear the leaked memory and restore email latency to normal levels, immediately resolving the checkout SLO breach. Based on RB-oom runbook.

suggested_actions.title: Increase email memory limit to buy investigation time
suggested_actions.rationale: If the leak recurs quickly after restart, raising the limit will extend the time before the next OOMKill, allowing more time to identify the leak source.

suggested_actions.title: Capture heap dump before next OOMKill for leak analysis
suggested_actions.rationale: Capture memory state to identify which objects are accumulating. Pattern matches PM-2026-05-04 where an unbounded cache caused the leak.

alternatives.why_less_likely: Payment 2.0.3 deployed 23m before the alert, but payment does not appear in the slow trace spans (trace 356ed282af89 shows only checkout→email). Payment's own metrics are not shown, and there's no evidence of payment errors or latency. The timing is coincidental.
